subject.title: Feature Request: Configurable Session Lane Concurrency + Auto-Yield

question: Should OpenClaw accept public same-session concurrency and auto-yield controls, and what scheduler contract should protect transcript ordering, tool side effects, and queued user messages?
rationale: Current core deliberately serializes each session and exposes cooperative yielding, so changing this adds public config surface and session-state semantics that automation cannot safely choose.

options.title: Design bounded scheduler mode
options.body: Define the session concurrency/auto-yield contract first, then implement it with schema, docs, upgrade proof, and regression coverage for ordering, cancellation, and delivery.

options.title: Keep serial sessions and improve fairness
options.body: Preserve one active writer per session while improving steering, interruption, or foreground-priority behavior to reduce perceived freezes without same-session parallel turns.

options.title: Split diagnostics only
options.body: Let the linked diagnostics PR handle the warning threshold and defer concurrency/auto-yield until maintainers decide the scheduler model.

recommendation.title: Design bounded scheduler mode
recommendation.body: Define the session concurrency/auto-yield contract first, then implement it with schema, docs, upgrade proof, and regression coverage for ordering, cancellation, and delivery.

likelyOwner.reason: The queue/concurrency history and existing ClawSweeper guidance point to this owner as the best available maintainer decision route.
